div.l: Accordeth noght as by his faculte
To haue wᵗith seke lasers acqueyntaunce
It is nought honest yt may nought auaunce
For to dele wᵗith soch poraylle
But all wᵗith ryche and sellers of vitaylle
And oủer all þere ꝓprofit shold aryse
Curteys he was and lowely of s̉eruyce
There was no man nowhere so v̉ertuous
He was þe best begger in his hous
For thogh a wydowe hade nought a sho
So plesaunt was his in principio
Yit wold he haue a ferthing ar he went
His purchas was wele bett̉er þan his rent
And rage he koude as it hade be a whelpe
In lovedayes þere koude he moch helpe
For þere he was nat like a cloysterer
Wᵗith a thredebare cope as is a poure scoler
But he was like a meister or a pope
Of double worstede was his semy cope
Rounde as ony belle out of þe presse
Somwhat he lysped for his wantonesse
To make his englissh swete on his tonge
And in his herpynge whan þat he hade songe .
His yen̄ twynkeld in his hede a ryght
As doth the steres in a frosty nyght
This worthy lymytour was cleped huberd
A marchaunt þere was wᵗith a forked berd
In motley and hye on hors he sat
And on his hede a flaundryssh beủer hat
His botes clasped feire and fetisly
His resons he spake full solempnely
Sownyng all wey þe encres of his wynnyng
He wold þe see were kept for ony thyng
Bitwene Mydelburgh and Orewell
Wele koude he in eschaunges sheldes sell
This worthy man full wele his wyt set
There wist no wight þat he was in det
So stedefastly did he of his goủernaunce
Wᵗith his b̄argeyns and wᵗith his cheuesaunce
For soth he was a worthy man wᵗith all
